name: assertR6
title: Returns the value when it passes the test whether the value is an R6 object with the requested slots

origin.description: Returns the value when it passes the test whether the value is an R6 object with the requested slots.
origin.usage: assertR6(x, classes = NULL, ordered = FALSE, cloneable = NULL, public = NULL, private = NULL, null.ok = FALSE, .var.name = vname(x), add = NULL)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Value under test. A Python int is an R integer and a Python float is an R double.

arguments.name: classes
arguments.text: Class names the object must inherit.

arguments.name: ordered
arguments.text: When true, the class names must appear in this order.

arguments.name: cloneable
arguments.text: When true the object must be cloneable, and when false it must not.

arguments.name: public
arguments.text: Names required in the public slots.

arguments.name: private
arguments.text: Names required in the private slots.

arguments.name: .var.name
arguments.text: Name used in the assertion message.

arguments.name: add
arguments.text: Collection that stores the message instead of stopping.

origin.details: Returns the value when it passes the test whether the value is an R6 object with the requested slots.
origin.value: The value when the check passes. Otherwise the check stops.
origin.example:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(checkmate))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(R6))
obj <- R6Class("Bar", public = list(a = 5))$new()
fn <- function(x) x
result <- assertR6(obj, "Bar", public = "a")
cat('R6\n')
